Everything here runs **inside your browser**. There is nothing to install, no
account to make, and nothing you can break. Each tutorial is self-contained ---
open it, work through it, close it.

If a page seems frozen when you first open it, give it a few seconds. R itself
is downloading.

::: {.tutorial-list}

### [Week 2 --- R Basics & The Weighted Dice](dice/)

Your first hour in R. Arithmetic and objects, vectors, functions and their
arguments, writing a function of your own, and running a simulation ten
thousand times --- ending with a pair of dice you have quietly weighted.

*Adapted from Grolemund,* Hands-On Programming with R, *ch. 1--3.*

### [Week 3 --- Working With an LLM, Part I: Prompt It](llm/)

Twenty minutes on the one skill that makes AI genuinely useful for code. You
will load a 229,444-row dataset and estimate a treatment effect, having been
taught neither --- and find out why *how* you ask decides whether you get an
answer or a fabrication.

*Uses Gerber, Green & Larimer (2008) on social pressure and voter turnout.*

:::
